subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and cross-channel explicit multi-bot mention semantics, or keep this as narrower memory-plugin and channel-plugin work?
rationale: The requested behavior changes memory authority, persisted storage shape, workspace-file precedence, conflict resolution, and channel delivery semantics; current main has useful pieces but no settled product contract for the proposed layer.

options.title: Keep as design tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-sponsored design that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation.

options.title: Split narrower work
options.body: Track Feishu self-mention loss and related bot-to-bot delivery as focused channel issues, and open separate memory-governance design only if maintainers want that direction.

options.title: Route through plugin APIs first
options.body: Require durable rule learning to prove it cannot be built through memory/plugin APIs before adding core rule-layer surface.

recommendation.title: Keep as design tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for maintainer-sponsored design that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the best available routing owner from the sampled history because the decision crosses the Feishu helper boundary, prompt/context authority, and core-vs-plugin policy.
